episodes.183034: A cutoff low produced multiple days of heavy rain. Hazards that resulted included gusty severe winds, flooding, funnel clouds, hail, and tree damage.
episodes.183851: An active pattern resulted in strong wind gusts in addition to isolated flash flooding to start the month of September.
episodes.185780: A deep closed low along the California coast and broad upper level ridging centered over the southern Plains promoted deep southerly flow across the Desert Southwest. This southerly flow promoted anomalous moisture advection into the area with PWATs upwards of 1.8-2 in the Lower Colorado River Valley area. Abundant moisture combined with CAPE upwards of 1,500-2,000 J/kg and a weak shortwave embedded in the flow allowed for efficient rain-producing thunderstorms to develop heading into the early afternoon hours on the 2nd. Several rain gages recorded over an inch of rainfall with these thunderstorms across southwest Arizona while radar estimates indicated locally heavier amounts in excess of 1.5 in some areas. As a result of these thunderstorms producing very heavy rainfall amounts in a short period of time, numerous instances of flash flooding occurred, particularly in the Yuma, Quartzsite, and Bouse areas. A couple of water rescues occurred, but no injuries were reported during this event.
episodes.185901: An upper level low pressure center situated over North Texas resulted in isolated to scattered thunderstorm development across North and East east Texas the afternoon of Sunday September 3. A few storms produced damaging winds and hail.
episodes.185933: Thunderstorms developed over the Cascades and drifted toward the Willamette Valley during the afternoon and evening.
episodes.186051: A push of monsoon moisture, which began in August, fueled thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. Several produced flash flooding, and one produced hail.
episodes.186142: An upper level low over northern California yielded a cooler,  wetter, and breezy pattern across the region through Labor Day weekend. Periods of light to moderate precipitation intermingled with isolated thunderstorms produced brief periods of heavy rainfall across the Sierra into northwest Nevada that caused some flash flooding and flooding concerns through the Labor weekend. Of particular concern was flooding in the playa area of the Black Rock Desert during the Burning Man festival.
episodes.186143: An upper level low over northern California yielded a cooler,  wetter, and breezy pattern across the region through Labor Day weekend. Periods of light to moderate precipitation intermingled with isolated thunderstorms produced brief periods of heavy rainfall across the Sierra into northwest Nevada that caused some flash flooding and flooding concerns through the Labor weekend. Of particular concern was flooding in the playa area of the Black Rock Desert during the Burning Man festival. A few isolated severe thunderstorms occurred across parts of the Basin and Range east of US-95 in Pershing, Churchill, and Mineral counties as well.

events.narrative: An image on social media showed elevated flow within Tyson Wash through La Paz Valley, making a low water crossing impassable. No damage or injuries were reported.
Interstate 15 was completely inundated between mile markers 4 and 7 and closed at the CA/NV state line.

A low water crossing through Tyson Wash along Kuehn Street was inundated by flash flooding, causing the road to be closed. Timing was estimated based on the stream gauge response located along Main Street. No damage or injuries were reported.

A stream gauge along Tyson Wash in Quartzsite observed a rapid rise, reaching Action stage at 1812MST. As a result, low water crossings along the wash were inundated and made impassable. No damage or injuries were reported.

A stream gauge located along Bouse Wash at Plomosa Road initially rose above Action stage around 1415MST as a result of flash flooding. The wash crested near moderate flood stage at 2150MST before eventually falling back below Action stage around 0730MST on the 3rd. No damage or injuries were reported.

A low water crossing through Tyson Wash along Quail Trail Street was inundated by flash flooding, causing the road to be close. Timing was estimated based on the Tyson Wash stream gauge response on Main Street. No damage or injuries were reported.
Storms training over the same area led to areal flooding over SR-305 in Lander County. The road was temporarily closed between MM 60 to MM 40.
Quartzsite Fire and Police performed a swift water rescue of two juveniles trapped on a small island in Tyson Wash. No injuries were reported.
Public report of 1 inch hail. No known report of damage. Duration of event estimated from radar.

A mesonet station (GW0802-Taylorsville) located 6.0 NW of Genesee, CA, a mesonet station (PIEC1-Pierce) located 5.0 mi NNW of Antelope Lake, CA, and mesonet station (QCSC1-Carman Saddle) located 4.0 mi SSW of Portola, CA, reported total rainfall amounts of 1.14, 0.89 and 0.85 inches respectively.
A trained spotter located 1.0 mi NE of Hawthorne, NV, reported a severe thunderstorm dropped several dime to half-inch size hailstones along with a few one-inch size hailstones.
Station (GGRN2) Giants Grave Raws, Elevation 4789 feet.
Public reported hail and heavy rain in Battle Mountain. Power also was out at time of report.

Heavy rain resulted in multiple mudslides and debris flows across U.S. Highway 191 between Helper and Duchesne, resulting in highway closure from milepost 259 to milepost 290 until the following morning.

The Utah Department of Transportation reported a significant debris flow over U.S. Highway 6 due to heavy rain over the Bear Fire burn scar area in Price Canyon, along with supporting video evidence. Due to the debris, the road remained closed into the following morning.
Zion National Park Rangers reported waterfalls occurring along streaked wall as you enter the Scenic Drive.

A CO-OP Observer located 1.6 mi S of Carson City, NV, and a CoCoRAHs Station (NV-CC-14) located 4.4 mi N of Carson City, NV, reported storm total rainfall amounts of 0.70 and 0.56 inches respectively.
The US-91 at MP 20 Wellsville mesonet station recorded a wind gust of 58 mph as a result of outflow winds associated with a nearby cluster of showers and thunderstorms moving through the area.

Nevada Department of Transportation (NDOT) reported flash flooding 5.0 mi N of Luning, NV. This event was initiated by a stronger  thunderstorm producing heavy rainfall and hail that caused debris flows and flooding across Nevada State Route 361. Nevada State Route 361 was closed briefly from 1:18 PM PST to 2:26 PM PST until NDOT opened one lane with a pilot car.
Flooding of all lanes occurred at East 4th street in Winnemucca near the intersection of Reinhardt street. This resulted from continuous heavy rain. Road remains closed as of 13:00 LT 9/4/23.
